name: What is the difference between painted, stained, and clear-coated cabinetry?

mainEntity.name: How do painted, stained, glazed, and clear-coated cabinet finishes compare for appearance, durability, and maintenance?
mainEntity.text: How do painted, stained, glazed, and clear-coated cabinet finishes compare for appearance, durability, and maintenance?

acceptedAnswer.text: The finish type changes both style and maintenance. Painted cabinetry offers a smooth, consistent look and is popular for clean, modern interiors, but it can show chips more obviously on edges and corners. Stained cabinets keep the wood grain visible and often work well in traditional, warm, or natural designs. Clear-coated cabinetry protects the wood while preserving its original tone, which is useful when the species itself is part of the design. Glazed finishes are typically used to add depth, shadow, or an aged effect, especially on detailed door profiles. For luxury projects, the most important factor is not the label but the finish system underneath: sanding, priming, sealing, curing, and topcoating all affect performance. If you are choosing for a busy kitchen, ask how easy each finish is to clean, repair, and touch up over time. The best choice balances design intent with how the room actually gets used.
acceptedAnswer.description: Painted cabinets give the most uniform look and work well for modern and transitional kitchens. Stained finishes highlight wood grain and natural variation, while clear coats preserve the raw wood appearance. Glazes add depth and dimension but can collect in detailed profiles. Durability depends more on the coating system and prep quality than on color alone.
